text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Attorney-General Amos Wako says Sheikh Khalid Balala is free to return to Kenya and sort out his residential status.
- Rioting Nairobi University students loot at least one shop while engaging in running battles with police during protests against a proposed Higher Education Bill.
- Opposition parliamentarian George Nyanja who escaped a bid to arrest him has gone underground.
- Politicians express mixed reactions over the planned pro-reform countrywide rallies planned for Monday by an opposition backed reform alliance.
- Parliament passes two bills and five tax measures contained in the financial statement for the year 1997/98 in a record 50 minutes.
- Professor Arthur Obel is given permission by the ministry of health to administer his controversial anti-AIDS drug Pearl Omega.
- The government embarks on a major rehabilitation programme of provincial general hospitals countrywide.
- The secretary-general of the opposition FORD-Asili Martin Shikuku says he will not endorse any of the party chairman's supporters for parliament in the coming general election.
- A cook in a Mombasa court is sentenced to hang for violently robbing a patron of 800 shillings.
- The Roman Catholic church in Kenya joins constitutional reform crusaders in calling for peaceful demonstrations at Nairobi's Kamkunji grounds on Monday.
- The 10 million shillings awarded to the president's aide Joshua Kulei against "The People" for libel, jolts Kenya's independent media to the hazards of journalism.
- A group of well-connected businessmen are engaged in an illegal multi-million shilling importation syndicate that uses forged Kenya Armed Forces documents. ($1=54.50 Kenyan Shillings)
